title: [recoverability] one spawn integrate per database for its life (a second start waits 15 s for a deploy's restart, then is refused naming the holder; a lock lost to another integrator stops it), and a gate script that is not there refuses the start (the 15:03 mission 9 halt)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 221 [recoverability] (mission 4 core; the lead's ask of 2026-11-18 15:4x after the 15:03 incident; scope YES at 16:0x with three conditions: 221.sh shows a deploy's restart still works and says whether systemd's Restart= retries a refused start; after landing the lead reads pg_locks that the unit's integrator holds the lock; no polled read added; author rev-f; readers rev-k first, rev-i second): one `spawn integrate` per database for its whole life, and a gate script that is not there refuses the start.

Why. At 15:03 a second `spawn integrate`, started by hand in ~/.local/share/spawn-rsi with SPAWN_GATE unset, judged mission 9. The integrator's advisory lock (integrator_try_lock) was taken per pass on a new connection and let go at every pass with no gate running, so a second integrator was never refused: it took every pass the unit's integrator left idle. Its gate was SPAWN_GATE's default, scripts/rsi/gate.sh resolved against its working directory, a file that is not there; every judging ran `sh <missing>`, an abort, and three aborts halted mission 9. FD 060's owner landing stalled 25 minutes.

What changes (crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs):
- At start, before the database is touched: the gate script must be a file the integrator can read (the gate runs it with sh). Otherwise exit 1 with, on stderr, "spawn: integrate: the gate script <path> does not exist (SPAWN_GATE is unset: its default scripts/rsi/gate.sh is read from the working directory <cwd>); this integrator does not start", "(from SPAWN_GATE)" when SPAWN_GATE named it, and "is not a readable file" for a directory or an unreadable file.
- Then the integrator's lock, on a connection of its own, before anything is written (the gate environment file included), kept for the process's life, idle or not (`--once` too; `--drain` unchanged). The connection is named "spawn integrate pid=<pid>" (application_name; the pid alone: the server keeps 63 bytes of a name).
- A start that finds the lock held says so ("integrate: another integrator holds this database's lock (<holder>); waiting up to 15 s for it to end") and asks every 0.5 s for 15 s, so a deploy's restart takes it. Still held after 15 s: exit 1, stderr "spawn: integrate: another integrator holds this database's lock (spawn integrate pid=<pid>, connected at <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS> UTC); this one does not start. Stop that one first, or drain it with `spawn integrate --drain --root <its root>`.", nothing recorded and no root made.
- After a failed pass the integrator reads once whether its connection still holds the lock, and keeps it if so. A connection that ended is dropped; the next pass asks for the lock on a new one. If another integrator holds it by then (not this pid's own old connection), exit 1: "spawn: integrate: this integrator's connection to the database ended and another integrator holds the lock now (<holder>); this one stops".
- Under the unit (Restart=always, RestartSec=10) a refused start is started again 10 s later, each start waiting its 15 s: systemd's start limit (5 in 10 s by default) is never reached. A stray integrator holding the lock makes the unit's integrator loop refused, the stray's pid named in the journal at every start: a stalled unit instead of aborted gates, by design.

What stays as it is: the lock's key (per database and schema), the integrator_down alert (it finds the lock held while idle too, never less), drain, gate units, the landing hold, the schema, every record kind. Nothing is read on every pass: pg_locks once after a failed pass, the holder once at a refused start or a refused re-take.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs; tests in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/database_tests.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/tests.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/tests/control.rs. Owner: rsi/scenarios/221.sh, rsi/backlog/221.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/221.sh, black box, a database of its own, no missions, stub gates (its header lists checks (1)-(6)):
- (1) an idle integrator A holds the lock, read from pg_locks five times over 2.5 s, its connection named by its pid;
- (2) a second start B exits 1 after its 15 s with the refusal naming A; no root made, no record written;
- (3) a deploy's restart: C started while A runs, A stopped 3 s later; C takes the lock within its 15 s;
- (4) a start with no gate script (SPAWN_GATE unset, a directory without scripts/rsi/gate.sh; and SPAWN_GATE naming a missing file) exits 1 with the gate refusal, before the lock, writing nothing;
- (5) C's connection ended on the server and F started: F takes the lock and C stops, exit 1, naming F.
- (4b, rev-k's R1 F1) SPAWN_GATE naming a directory: exit 1 with "is not a readable file (from SPAWN_GATE)", no root made;
- (4c, rev-i's R2 F1) SPAWN_GATE naming a regular file of mode 000: exit 1 with "is not a readable file (from SPAWN_GATE)", no root made (a harness failure under a user who reads it anyway, root);
- (6, rev-k's R1 F2) F's passes failing on a live connection (spawn_now_ms renamed): F keeps the lock, so G is refused at 15 s naming F.
On live main 08c8138b, 221.sh exits 1.

Tests (unit): a second integrator refused while the first is idle, including after a pass that failed on a live connection; a start that takes a lock freed within its wait; a lock held for life lost only to another integrator; the gate script refusals; the store's holder read and holds-lock read.

Verified by: after landing, the lead reads pg_locks read-only: the unit's integrator holds the lock (class 1399957336), its connection named "spawn integrate pid=<the unit's MainPID>".
